messages:
Maya (docs): Heads-up — I noticed the generate endpoint examples in the API ref send request metadata as `headers: { \"client_id\": \"...\" }` but our JS SDK sends `x-client-id` as a header. Customers are confused and the curl example in the OpenAPI page is inconsistent.

Dan (eng): Yikes, thanks for flagging. Server currently accepts both `client_id` in JSON body && `x-client-id` header for legacy reasons, but examples should show the recommended approach which is `x-client-id` header. We recently added an alias param `client_metadata` that muddled the docs.

Sam (sdk): Confirmed on SDK side — JS and Go SDKs map `clientId` -> `x-client-id` header. The Python snippet in docs shows `client_id` inside the request body which is wrong. I'll paste the Go example we use:```go
req.Header.Set("x-client-id", "acme-123")
resp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, req)
```

Oliver (pm): Can we do a small docs PR that: 1) standardizes to `x-client-id` in curl/js/go/python examples, 2) adds migration note for folks still using `client_id` in body, and 3) adds a short sentence in the param table explaining the alias? ETA? @Dan / @Sam

Dan (eng): I'll verify behavior across versions. Quick note: streaming SSE examples also include metadata lines like `event: metadata\ndata: {"client_id":"..."}` — those should be `x-client-id` too. I can update the runtime to normalize incoming body `client_id` to an internal header if we want a backward-compatible server-side fix, but that's a small change and needs a canary.

Maya (docs): I'll open a docs PR with the edits and example swaps. Need the exact text for the migration note and a canonical curl + python + js snippet. Sam, can you drop the Python and JS snippets here so I can copy? :pray: :sparkles:

Sam (sdk): Sure. JS snippet (fetch):```js
fetch("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer $TOKEN",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "x-client-id": "acme-123"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: "redwood/gpt-3" })
})
```

Python snippet:```py
import requests
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "x-client-id": "acme-123"}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json={"model":"redwood/gpt-3"}, headers=headers)
```

Dan (eng): For the migration blurb: "Note: older integrations may pass client identifiers in the request body using `client_id`. We recommend migrating to the `x-client-id` header. The server currently accepts the body field for backwards compatibility, but this behavior is scheduled for deprecation in Q3 2025; updating to the header ensures consistent routing and observability." Feel free to tweak wording.

Oliver (pm): Q3 2025 deprecation note sounds good. Add a short example showing the old vs new and a one-line impact: "Observability and routing rely on header-based metadata."

Maya (docs): Great — I'll include Dan's text and Sam's snippets. I'll also update the SSE streaming example to show metadata as headers and streaming `event: chunk` frames unchanged. I'll open PR in ~30m and tag @Dan @Sam for review.

deploy-bot: deploy status: no recent runtime changes to normalize `client_id` -> header (branch: main). Latest canary: build/9241 passed.

Dan (eng): Thanks. If we decide to normalize server-side we should coordinate a rollout; for now docs-only change is safest. :thumbsup:

Maya (docs): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/478 — includes curl/js/py/go swaps + migration note + SSE example. Tagging reviewers. :sparkles:

Sam (sdk): Reviewing now. If small, we can ship within the hour. I'll check Go code snippet for exact import names.

Oliver (pm): Awesome — once merged let's add a tiny changelog entry so customers see the clarification.

Maya (docs): Will do. Thanks everyone! :tada:
